# Ezra Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 469r–469v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** And-heard the-adversaries [tsarei] of-Yehudah and-Binyamin that the-sons of-the-exile [benei ha-golah] were-building a-temple [hekhal] to-YHWH the-God of-Yisra'el.

**4:2** And-they-drew-near [vayigshu] to Zerubbavel and-to the-heads of-the-fathers [rashei ha-avot] and-said to-them, "Let-us-build with-you, for like-you we-seek [nidrosh] your-God, and-to-him we have-been-sacrificing [anachnu zovechim] since the-days of-Esar-Chaddon [Esarhaddon] king of-Ashur [Assyria] who-brought-us-up [he'elanu] here."

**4:3** And-said to-them Zerubbavel and-Yeshua and-the-rest of-the-heads of-the-fathers of-Yisra'el, "Not to-you and-to-us to-build a-house to-our-God, for we ourselves together [anachnu yachad] will-build to-YHWH the-God of-Yisra'el, as the-king Koresh king of-Paras commanded-us."

**4:4** And-it-was the-people of-the-land [am ha-arets] weakening [meraphim] the-hands of-the-people of-Yehudah and-terrifying-them [mevalhalim otam] from-building,

**4:5** and-hiring against-them counselors [yoatsim] to-frustrate [lehapher] their-plan [atsatam] all the-days of-Koresh king of-Paras and-until the-reign of-Daryavesh [Darius] king of-Paras.

**4:6** And-in-the-reign of-Achashverosh [Ahasuerus], in-the-beginning of-his-reign, they-wrote an-accusation [sitnah] against the-inhabitants of-Yehudah and-Yerushalayim.

**4:7** And-in-the-days of-Artachshasta [Artaxerxes], wrote Bishlam, Mitredat, Tav'el, and-the-rest of-their-companions [kenavatav], to Artachshasta king of-Paras; and-the-writing [ketav] of-the-letter [ha-nishtavan] was-written in-Aramit [Aramaic] and-translated [u-meturgam] in-Aramit.

**4:8** Rechum the-commander [be'el te'em] and-Shimshai the-scribe [saphera] wrote a-letter [iggera] against Yerushalayim to-Artachshasta the-king, as-follows [ki-dna]:

**4:9** Then Rechum the-commander and-Shimshai the-scribe and-the-rest of-their-companions: the-judges [dinaye], the-governors [apharsathkhaye], the-officials [tarpelaye], the-Persians [Pharsa'e], the-men-of-Erekh [Arkhevaye], the-Babylonians [Bavlaye], the-Susians [Shushankhaye] — that is the-Elamites [Elama'e] —

**4:10** and-the-rest of-the-nations [ummayya] which the-great and-noble [yaqira] Osnappar [Ashurbanipal] exiled [hagli] and-settled-them [hotiv himmow] in-the-city of-Shomron [Samaria] and-the-rest of-the-region-Beyond-the-River [Avar-Nahara], and-now [ukh'enet]:

**4:11** This [is] the-copy [parshegen] of-the-letter that they-sent to-him — to Artachshasta the-king: "Your-servants, the-men of-the-region-Beyond-the-River, and-now:

**4:12** Let-it-be-known to-the-king that the-Yehuda'in [Jews] who came-up from-beside-you [min-lvatakh] have-come to-us, to-Yerushalayim. The-rebellious [maradata] and-wicked [bishta] city they-are-building [bonin], and-the-walls [shurayya] they-have-completed [shakhliluv], and-the-foundations [ushayya] they-are-repairing [yachituw].

**4:13** Now let-it-be-known to-the-king that if this city is-built and-the-walls completed [yishtakhlelun], tax [mindah], tribute [velo], and-toll [halakh] they-will-not give [la yintenun], and-the-revenue of-kings [apptom di malakhin] it-will-harm [tehanzeq].

**4:14** Now because the-salt of-the-palace [melach hekhala] we-eat [melachna], and-the-dishonor [aryat] of-the-king [is] not-fitting [la arakh] for-us to-see, therefore we-have-sent and-made-known to-the-king,

**4:15** that search-may-be-made [yevaqar] in-the-book [sepher] of-the-records [dakranayya] of-your-fathers, and-you-will-find in-the-book of-the-records and-will-know that this city [is] a-rebellious [maradata] city, and-harmful [mahanzeqat] to-kings and-provinces [medintan], and-revolt [eshtatdur] they-have-made in-its-midst from-days of-old [yomat alma]. Therefore this city was-destroyed [hachrovat].

**4:16** We make-known to-the-king that if this city is-built and-its-walls completed, by-reason-of-this a-portion [chalaq] in-the-region-Beyond-the-River you-will-not have [la itai lakh]."

**4:17** The-king sent an-answer [pitgama]: "To-Rechum the-commander and-Shimshai the-scribe and-the-rest of-their-companions who-dwell in-Shomron and-the-rest of-the-region-Beyond-the-River — peace [shelam], and-now:

**4:18** The-letter that you-sent to-us has-been-read [mefarash qeri] before-me.

**4:19** And-a-command [te'em] was-issued by-me, and-they-searched [ve-vaqaru] and-found that this city from-days of-old against kings has-risen-up [mitnasse'ah], and-rebellion [merad] and-revolt [eshtadur] has-been-made in-it.

**4:20** And-mighty [taqifin] kings have-been over Yerushalayim and-ruling [shallitin] over all the-region-Beyond-the-River, and-tax, tribute, and-toll was-given [mityhev] to-them.

**4:21** Now issue [simu] a-command [te'em] to-make-these men cease [le-vatala], and-this city shall-not be-built until a-command [te'em] is-issued [yitsam] by-me.

**4:22** And-take-heed [u-zehirin hevow] not to-be negligent [shaluw] in-this; why should-damage-increase [yisgeh] to-the-injury [la-hatsalat] of-kings?"

**4:23** Then when the-copy [parshegen] of-the-letter of-Artachshasta the-king was-read before Rechum and-Shimshai the-scribe and-their-companions, they-went in-haste [bivhilu] to-Yerushalayim to-the-Yehuda'in and-made-them-cease [batilu himmow] by-force [bi-dra] and-power [ve-chayil].

**4:24** Then ceased [betelat] the-work of-the-house of-God which [is] in-Yerushalayim, and-it-was-stopped [va-havat batela] until the-year two of-the-reign of-Daryavesh king of-Paras.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.7 — Language shift to Aramaic:** From 4:8 through 6:18, the text switches from Hebrew to Aramaic (the diplomatic language of the Persian empire). This is not a gloss — the author preserves the official correspondence in its administrative language. The phrase *ketav ha-nishtavan katuv Aramit u-meturgam Aramit* ("the writing of the letter was written in Aramaic and translated in Aramaic") signals this transition.

**v.10 — "Osnappar the great and noble":** This is likely Ashurbanipal (668-627 BCE), the last great Assyrian king, here given a flattering epithet (*rav ve-yaqira*) that may reflect the diplomatic register of the letter rather than the author's own view.

**v.12-16 — The accusation conflates temple and walls:** The letter strategically blurs the distinction between rebuilding the temple (which Cyrus authorized) and rebuilding the city walls (which had military implications). This rhetorical sleight is central to the opposition's strategy.

*— EMET*
